area: Logistics Manager & Pricing Manager meta-roles (Buildings.Office.Headquarters) — the multi-store "manager plan" pattern
findings:
OVERVIEW / TWO DIFFERENT "MULTI-STORE" MODELS
Both roles are "HQ manager plans": a plain C# plan object stored on the save, an employee slot on that plan, and a BizMan tab in the Headquarters business that renders it. They differ in how "multiple stores" is expressed:
- Pricing Manager: IMPLICIT set. One plan supervises one NEIGHBORHOOD; GetSupervisedStores() = every player-rented revenue-generating business in that neighborhood. No add/remove-store UI, no numeric cap. One plan per neighborhood.
- Logistics Manager: EXPLICIT list. plan.destinations is an ordered List<LogisticsManagerPlanDestination>; the player adds one entry per target business and configures per-destination product stock targets. Only the first MaxDestinations entries are active; MaxDestinations is skill-scaled. This per-destination-with-limits shape is the closest analogue to the mod's "assign N stores + set limits per store".

===== 1. WHERE PLANS ARE STORED / SERIALIZED =====
GameInstance.cs (the root save object, = SaveGameManager.Current) holds hard-coded lists:
  public List<LogisticsManagerPlan> logisticsManagerPlans = new();   (GameInstance.cs:218)
  public List<HeadhunterPlan> headhunterPlans;                        (:220)
  public List<HrManagerPlan> hrManagerPlans;                          (:222)
  public List<PricingManagerPlan> pricingManagerPlans = new();        (:224)
Plans are POCOs (PricingManagerPlan / LogisticsManagerPlan have NO [Serializable] attribute themselves; LogisticsManagerPlanDestination and the EmployeeInstance subclasses do). They are serialized only as members of GameInstance.
Serializer = SaveGameSerializationHelper.cs: OdinSerializer binary (SerializationUtility.SerializeValue, DataFormat.Binary) using Player.SaveSystem.SaveGameSerializationPolicy (ISerializationPolicy wrapping SerializationPolicies.Unity, and it SKIPS any member marked [Obsolete]). A Newtonsoft JSON path also exists (JsonConvert, TypeNameHandling.Auto, ReferenceLoopHandling.Ignore) plus a legacy BinaryFormatter fallback.
Consequences: public fields serialize; `readonly string id = UuidHelper.GenerateBase64Uuid()` serializes; private runtime caches (PricingManagerPlan._supervisedStoresCache, _supervisedStoresCacheFrame, _snapshottedPrices; the static Dictionaries on LogisticsManagerPlan) are NOT serialized under the Unity policy. [FormerlySerializedAs] is used for renamed fields (LogisticsManagerPlan.targetAddress ex "warehouseAddress"; LogisticsManagerPlanDestination.deliveryTargetAddress ex "targetBusinessAddress").
On load, ICompatibilityFix passes sanitize the lists: InitializePricingManagerPlans (null-guard), UpdateLogisticsManagerPlans (recompute isFactory, prune destinations of wrong business type), RemoveInvalidPlans / RemoveOrphanedPricingManagerPlans / UpdateHeadquartersPlansToNewSystem (drop plans whose HQ or warehouse is no longer RentedByPlayer; null out EmployeeInstance.assignedHrManagerPlanId dangling refs).

===== 2. SUPERVISED STORES: implementation, add/remove UI, cap =====
PRICING — PricingManagerPlan.GetSupervisedStores() (private, PricingManagerPlan.cs:384): iterates SaveGameManager.Current.BuildingRegistrations, keeps those where IsSupervisedStore(reg) == PricingManagerHelper.IsManageableBusiness(reg) && reg.Neighborhood == plan.supervisedNeighborhood. IsManageableBusiness = reg.RentedByPlayer && reg.retailPrices != null && BusinessTypeHelper.GetData(reg).HasTag(generatesrevenue). Result cached per-frame (_supervisedStoresCacheFrame == Time.frameCount).
  Add/remove UI: there is NONE per store. The only control is the neighborhood dropdown in PricingManagerPlanUI (neighborhoodDropdown -> OnChangedNeighborhood -> plan.SetSupervisedNeighborhood(nb)). SetSupervisedNeighborhood(): RestoreOriginalPrices(); clears appliedPrices/manuallyPricedItems; sets supervisedNeighborhood; invalidates cache; SnapshotCurrentPrices(); RecomputeSuggestions(). PricingManagerPlanUI.GetSelectableNeighborhoods filters out neighborhoods already covered by another plan (PricingManagerHelper.IsNeighborhoodSupervised(nb, exceptPlanId)). PricingManagersPlanList shows an "owned businesses: N" label (GetOwnedBusinessCount).
  Cap: no count cap. Skill (PricingManagerSkillValue 0-100) only affects price-suggestion quality (see PricingManagerHelper.ComputeSuggestion + PricingManagerSettings.minSkillCapture/captureJitter/visibleSpread).

LOGISTICS — LogisticsManagerPlan has NO GetSupervisedStores(); it has destinations: List<LogisticsManagerPlanDestination> (public field, LogisticsManagerPlan.cs:41). GetPlannedDeliveries() (iterator, :52) yields destinations[0..min(MaxDestinations, destinations.Count)] but ONLY if: targetAddress defined, assignedEmployeeId != null, MaxDestinations != 0, LogisticsManagerInstance.IsEmployeeAvailable(), and the source Warehouse is still RentedByPlayer (else it nulls targetAddress).
  Add/remove UI: LogisticsManagerPlanUI.AddDestination() -> destinations.Add(new LogisticsManagerPlanDestination{isUiCollapsed=false}); addDestinationButton.interactable = destinations.Count < plan.MaxDestinations. Each destination rendered by LogisticsManagerDestinationUI: a businessTargetDropdown of eligible player buildings (LogisticsManagerPlanUI.Destinations, built via BuildingHelper.GetPlayerBuildingRegistrations with tag filter iswarehousedestination / isfactorydestination, + import/export for factory plans); removeButton -> HudConfirm -> destinations.RemoveAt(i). Reorderable list (destinationsReorderableList) — order matters because only the first MaxDestinations are active; entries beyond the cap render at 0.5 alpha.
  Cap: LogisticsManagerPlan.MaxDestinations => CalculateMaxDestinations(targetAddress, assignedEmployeeId) (:43,:145): base = ((Warehouse)reg).vehicleSlots.Sum(slot.DestinationsThatCanDeliver); if base==0 return 0; skill = EmployeeHelper.GetSkillOfEmployee(employeeId,"ba:skill_logisticsmanager"); return base + floor(base * skill/100). So a 100-skill manager doubles destination capacity. GetMaxPossibleDestinations = base*2 (used for warnings). Changing to a lower-skill manager when destinations.Count exceeds the new max pops a HudConfirm ("bizman_logisticsmanager_lower_skill_confirm" / "..._max_capacity_exceeded_confirm").

===== 3. THE MANAGER EMPLOYEE: assignment + where it lives =====
The employee is a NORMAL hired employee in GameInstance.EmployeeInstances ("My Employees"), of a concrete subclass:
  Entities/LogisticsManager.cs : EmployeeInstance ; Entities/PricingManager.cs : EmployeeInstance ; Entities/HRManager.cs, Entities/Headhunter.cs.
  RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate(skillName,...) (RecruitmentHelper.cs:41) switch: "ba:skill_logisticsmanager" => new LogisticsManager(), "ba:skill_pricingmanager" => new PricingManager(), "ba:skill_hrmanager" => new HRManager(), "ba:skill_headhunter" => new Headhunter(), _ => new EmployeeInstance(). So you HIRE it through the ordinary recruitment flow (recruitment agency / job listing filtered to that skill), it gets assignedAddress = the HQ, and it draws a normal daily wage via EmployeeHelper.PayDailyWages / EmployeeInstance.PayWage.
  There is NO "hire manager" button on the plan. AddPlan() just does `new XxxManagerPlan { headquartersAddress = bizMan.business.address }` (free, no employee). The employee is attached afterward via a per-plan manager DROPDOWN.
  Assignment call sites:
    Pricing: PricingManagersPlanList.UpdatePricingManagerDropdownForPlan builds candidates = EmployeeInstances where assignedAddress == HQ && HasSkill("ba:skill_pricingmanager") && !PricingManagerHelper.IsEmployeeAssignedToOtherPlan(id, plan.id) && IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift(). Selecting -> plan.AssignEmployee(id) (PricingManagerPlan.AssignEmployee: sets assignedEmployeeId, SnapshotCurrentPrices, ReapplyPrices, RecomputeSuggestions) / plan.UnAssignEmployee() (RestoreOriginalPrices, null id, clear suggestions).
    Logistics: LogisticsManagersPlanList.UpdateLogisticsManagerDropdownForPlan candidates = EmployeeInstances where assignedAddress == HQ && HasSkill("ba:skill_logisticsmanager") && not on another logistics plan && IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift(). Selecting sets plan.assignedEmployeeId directly (+ SaveGameManager.MarkChange()).
  Desk / workstation: YES it needs one, indirectly. IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() (EmployeeInstance.cs:302) for a non-driver requires a WorkShift whose row exists in the HQ schedule. Schedule rows come from ScheduleHelper.FetchWorkstations() -> BuildingRegistration.GetAssignableItems(): an item is a workstation iff itemCached.assignable && one of itemCached.suitableSkills is in (HQ businessType.employeePrimarySkills + buildingType.requiredBuildingSkills). ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation checks the employee's skills against WorkstationsById[id].ItemCached.suitableSkills. So the HQ must contain a "manager desk" item whose suitableSkills includes ba:skill_logisticsmanager / ba:skill_pricingmanager, and the manager must be scheduled onto it.
  If the manager stops being scheduled, ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans() (called on every HQ schedule edit, and from ScheduleAutoFillerHelper for HQ) auto-clears plan.assignedEmployeeId / calls plan.UnAssignEmployee(). Employee.UnAssignWork() (on resign/reset) also detaches: LogisticsManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForEmployee(id)?.UnAssignEmployee(), PricingManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForPricingManager(id)?.UnAssignEmployee().

===== 4. SCHEDULED vs ALWAYS-ON =====
Scheduling is an ELIGIBILITY GATE, not an activity window.
- You must inrooster the manager in the HQ schedule (a WorkShift on a suitable workstation) for it to be assignable to a plan; UpdateHQPlans() enforces this continuously.
- But the actual work does NOT gate on shift hours:
  Logistics: fires from GameManager.RunMainGameTick when Hour == 2 (GameManager.cs:623-636): LogisticsManagerHelper.DoAllFactoryDeliveries() then DoAllWarehouseDeliveries(), regardless of whether hour 2 is inside the manager's shift. Only gate inside GetPlannedDeliveries is LogisticsManagerInstance.IsEmployeeAvailable() (= not absent, or absent-but-replaced; not "on shift now").
  Pricing: PricingManagerHelper.RunHourly() (GameManager.cs:617, every game hour) -> for each plan with assignedEmployeeId && plan.IsUpdateDue() -> plan.RunUpdate(). "Due" is plan.nextUpdateDay/nextUpdateHour vs TimeHelper; cadence from PricingManagerSettings (updateHour default 8, hoursBetweenUpdates default 24). Not tied to the shift.
- Note: LogisticsManager and PricingManager do NOT override EmployeeInstance.WorkDaily()/WorkHourly() (only HRManager does — it calls plan.TrainEmployees()/PayHealthInsurance() from EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily()). Logistics/Pricing work is driven purely by the GameManager tick hooks above.

===== 5. WHAT THE MANAGER DOES EACH TICK + CALLERS =====
LOGISTICS (source = a player Warehouse or Factory; NOT DeliveryContracts):
  Caller chain: GameManager.RunMainGameTick (Hour==2) -> LogisticsManagerHelper.DoAllWarehouseDeliveries()/DoAllFactoryDeliveries() -> foreach plan (filtered by isFactory) foreach plan.GetPlannedDeliveries() -> WarehouseDeliveriesWork/FactoryDeliveriesWork.Enqueue(PlanDestinationPair). DistributedWork queues are progressed frame-by-frame in RunMainGameTick (GameManager.cs:455-460) -> ProgressDelivery -> pair.plan.DeliverDestination(pair.destination); when both queues drained -> LogisticsManagerPlan.OnFinishedDeliveries().
  LogisticsManagerPlan.DeliverDestination: casts targetAddress to Warehouse; destination.Deliver(warehouse, isImportExport, out undeliveredNoStock, out undeliveredNoShelves). LogisticsManagerPlanDestination.Deliver: for each ItemAmountTarget stockTarget -> ProcessStockTarget: for a normal store destination it computes num2 = stockTarget.targetAmount - BuildingHelper.CountTotalResourcesInStock(destAddr, item) (i.e. TOP UP the store to the target), withdraws that many from the warehouse cargo (BuildingHelper.WithdrawFromCargo), ItemHelper.DeliverCargoToBuilding onto PointOfSale/ShowcaseShelf then StorageShelf; leftover with no shelf space -> undeliveredNoShelves; not enough warehouse stock -> undeliveredNoStock. Creates warehouse.deliveryTransactions entries (DeliveryTransaction) — this is where cargo/vehicle movement + cost is modelled. For factory->importexport destinations it instead SELLS (ProductMarketHelper.GetProductExportPrice; accumulates importExportProfits -> LogisticsManagerPlan.PendingTransactions -> GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe in OnFinishedDeliveries via TransactionInfo "ba:transaction_exportedgoods"; also warehouse.factoryExports). After delivering it also calls BusinessHelper.FillUpEmptyShowcaseShelvesAndPointsOfSales(destAddr) and sets GameManager.shouldUpdateAfterDeliveries.
  OnFinishedDeliveries: SendDeliveryReport for each plan that had shortfalls -> Contact.EnsurePermanentContact("logistics_alerts", ContactCategoryName.ImportsAndGoods, ...).SendMessage(new TextMessage("ba:messagetype_phone_logistics_manager_delivery_no_stock" / "..._no_available_space", data)); applies PendingTransactions; NotifyDeliveryAlerts() -> Notifications.Show(Warning, "delivery_alert_notification"/"..._multiple", onClick -> open the logistics_alerts contact).
  It does NOT read/modify DeliveryContract, DeliveryHelper, repeatingOrder, wholesale at all (grep of the whole Headquarters folder for DeliveryContract = 0 hits). The wholesale/DeliveryContract system is the separate BusinessHelper.HandleWholesaleDeliveries() called right after.

PRICING (writes retail prices across all stores in the neighborhood):
  Caller: GameManager hourly -> PricingManagerHelper.RunHourly() -> plan.RunUpdate() when due.
  PricingManagerPlan.RunUpdate(): (nextUpdateDay,nextUpdateHour)=PricingManagerHelper.GetNextUpdateTime(); RecomputeSuggestions(); ReapplyManagedPrices(); NotifyMispricedItems().
  RecomputeSuggestions(): normalizedSkill = PricingManagerSkillValue/100; for each sellable item across supervised stores -> BuildSuggestion -> PricingManagerHelper.ComputeSuggestion(item, supervisedNeighborhood, normalizedSkill, stable-RNG jitter) returns (min,max) in currency; stored in cachedSuggestions (PriceSuggestion{itemName, suggestedMin, suggestedMax, rivalReferencePrice, isPlayerSelling, sellingBusinessTypes}). Ceiling = ItemHelper.CalculateMaxAcceptablePriceByNeighborhood capped 10000; higher skill -> closer to ceiling, less jitter, narrower visible range.
  ReapplyManagedPrices(): for each cachedSuggestion NOT in manuallyPricedItems -> ReapplyPriceWhereSold(item, suggestedMax): for each GetSupervisedStores() that stocks/sells the item -> SnapshotOriginalPrice(store,item) (into originalStorePrices for later restore) then SetPrice -> writes BOTH store.retailPrices and store.storedRetailPrices lists (RetailPrice{itemName,price}); records into plan.appliedPrices. ApplyPriceToStores also calls ProductMarketHelper.UpdateMarketDemand(item) when a new price row is created.
  NotifyMispricedItems(): counts manuallyPricedItems priced above PricingManagerHelper.GetHighestAcceptableCents -> Notifications.Show(Info, "notifications_PricingManager_mispriced_items", {employeeName, amount}, onClick -> open BizMan "PricingManagers" tab and select this plan).
  Player-driven price application (not tick): PricingManagerProductCellView.ApplyPrice -> plan.ApplyManualPrice(item, price) (pins it in manuallyPricedItems); PricingManagerProductsScrollerController "Apply suggested prices" button -> foreach visible model plan.ApplySuggestedPrice(item, suggestedMax) (un-pins).
  On UnAssignEmployee / SetSupervisedNeighborhood / Delete -> RestoreOriginalPrices() rewrites store.retailPrices/storedRetailPrices back from originalStorePrices (only for stores still RentedByPlayer).

===== 6. EXACT PLAYER-SET CONFIG (the "limits") =====
LogisticsManagerPlan fields:
  string id (readonly, uuid)
  string assignedEmployeeId
  Address headquartersAddress
  Address targetAddress   [FormerlySerializedAs "warehouseAddress"] — the SOURCE warehouse/factory (dropdown: warehouseDropdown)
  bool isFactory — which sub-tab ("Warehouse" vs "Factory"); also selects destination filter + top-up-vs-deliver-up-to semantics
  List<LogisticsManagerPlanDestination> destinations — ordered; first MaxDestinations active
LogisticsManagerPlanDestination fields (THE per-store limits):
  Address deliveryTargetAddress   [FormerlySerializedAs "targetBusinessAddress"] — which store (dropdown businessTargetDropdown)
  List<ItemAmountTarget> stockTargets — per product: { string itemName; int targetAmount (0..9,999,999) }. For a store destination targetAmount = "minimum stock amount" (manager tops the store up to it); for a factory destination = "deliver up to". Editable via input field + / - buttons per product row (LogisticsManagerPlanUI.LoadProducts). targetAmount==0 removes the target.
  bool isUiCollapsed — pure UI state
  (no per-destination budget cap — the only "budget" limiter is warehouse stock on hand and MaxDestinations)
Global (dev-tunable, not per plan): there is no LogisticsManagerSettings ScriptableObject.

PricingManagerPlan fields:
  string id (readonly)
  string assignedEmployeeId
  Address headquartersAddress
  string supervisedNeighborhood — the ONE setting the player picks (dropdown)
  List<OriginalStorePrice> originalStorePrices — snapshot {storeAddress, itemName, hadPrice, price, hadStoredPrice, storedPrice} for restore
  List<RetailPrice> appliedPrices — {itemName, price} the manager last applied
  HashSet<string> manuallyPricedItems — items the player pinned; excluded from auto-repricing
  int nextUpdateDay, int nextUpdateHour — recompute cursor
  List<PriceSuggestion> cachedSuggestions
Per-product player input (PricingManagerProductCellView): a manual price per item (pins), or accept suggested (bulk button); PricingManagerFilterController / PricingManagerFilterToggle filter which business-types/products are shown & bulk-applied.
Global PricingManagerSettings (ScriptableObject, InstanceBehavior<GlobalReferences>.pricingManagerSettings — NOT per plan, shared):
  float minSkillCapture (0..1) — how close a 0-skill analyst gets to the best price
  float captureJitter (0..0.5, default 0.15) — per-product random downward miss, vanishes at 100 skill
  float visibleSpread (0..0.5) — width of the shown price range, vanishes at 100 skill
  int updateHour (0..23, default 8)
  int hoursBetweenUpdates (1..24, default 24)
  bool applyOnlyToVisibleProducts (default true)

For comparison, HrManagerPlan (the count-capped pattern) config: assignedEmployeeId, headquartersAddress, List<string> assignedEmployees, bool replaceAbsentEmployees, int trainingTarget (default 50), HealthInsurancePlan healthInsurancePlan; MaxEmployees => HrManagerSkillValue.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees(). This is the model to copy if the mod wants a skill-scaled numeric store cap.

===== 7. EVERY UI CLASS THAT RENDERS THE PLAN =====
Tab host: BizManBusiness.cs — SetUpTabs() hard-codes, for businesstype_headquarters, the tab list: Schedule, PricingManagers, LogisticsManagers, PurchasingAgents, HRManagers, Headhunters, Settings. Tab GameObjects are prefab children of `menu` / `containers`; constants BizMan.PricingManagersTab / LogisticsManagersTab. HeadquartersList.cs adds a per-skill count badge on the HQ card: SetUpEmployeeCounter(entry, addr, "PricingManagers", "ba:skill_pricingmanager") and ("LogisticsManagers","ba:skill_logisticsmanager").
Pricing UI (namespace UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PricingManagers):
  PricingManagersPlanList (plan list for the HQ: AddPlan/reorder/delete, per-row manager dropdown, "owned businesses: N" label; SelectPlanById used by notification click)
  PricingManagersPlanListEntry (row: manager name, neighborhood name, selected state, ManagerDropdown)
  PricingManagerPlanUI (neighborhoodDropdown + productsScroller; hosts NoManagerAssignedPopUp)
  PricingManagerProductsScrollerController ("applySuggestedPricesButton", builds product cell list, ApplyTargets respects applyOnlyToVisibleProducts)
  PricingManagerProductCellView (per product: current / suggested / rival price, priceInput -> ApplyManualPrice)
  PricingManagerProductModel (view model: CurrentPrice via plan.TryGetUniformPrice, SuggestedPrice, RivalsPrice)
  PricingManagerFilterController, PricingManagerFilterToggle (business-type filters)
Logistics UI (namespace UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.LogisticsManagers):
  LogisticsManagersPlanList (Warehouse/Factory sub-tabs via ChangeTab; plan list; AddPlan; reorderable; per-row manager dropdown; NoManagerAssignedPopUp wiring)
  LogisticsManagersPlanListEntry (row: SetManager/SetLocationName, ManagerDropdown)
  LogisticsManagerPlanUI (warehouseDropdown = source; addDestinationButton; destinationsReorderableList; "deliver to N destinations" label; ShowWarehouse; per-product runs-out-in / export-price columns)
  LogisticsManagerDestinationUI (per destination: businessTargetDropdown, collapse/remove, product stock-target rows with +/- and input)
  LogisticsManagerListSortable / LogisticsManagerListEntryData / LogisticsManagerListOption (the sortable product sub-list: ProductName, WarehouseStock, RunsOutIn, BusinessTarget, CargoAmount)
Shared: NoManagerAssignedPopUp (shown when plan has no assigned employee; embeds an employee dropdown + delete-plan). HudConfirm (confirmations). Notifications / UI.Notification.Notifications. Contacts: Contact "logistics_alerts" thread (ContactsApp, ContactCategoryName.ImportsAndGoods) for delivery failure phone messages.
Tutorial gating classes (read plan state): TutorialPointerHideConditionHasPricingManagerPlan, HasPricingManagerPlan, TutorialPointerHideConditionHasAssignedPricingManager, TutorialPointerHideConditionHasSupervisedNeighborhood, TutorialPointerHideConditionHasLogisticsManagerPlan, HasLogisticsManagerDestination, HasAnyTypeOfDeliveriesOnTakenOverBusiness, TutorialPointerHeadquartersPlanHelper.

===== HELPERS (static, the mod's likely integration surface) =====
PricingManagerHelper: Settings, RunHourly(), GetNextUpdateTime(), AddPlan(plan), GetPlanFromId(id), GetPlansForHeadquarters(addr), GetAssignedPlanForPricingManager(empId), IsEmployeeAssignedToOtherPlan(empId,exceptId), IsNeighborhoodSupervised(nb,exceptId), GetPlanCoveringNeighborhood(nb), IsManageableBusiness(reg), DeletePlan(id), GetHighestAcceptableCents, ComputeSuggestion.
LogisticsManagerHelper: DoAllWarehouseDeliveries(), DoAllFactoryDeliveries(), WarehouseDeliveriesWork/FactoryDeliveriesWork (DistributedWork), GetAssignedPlanForEmployee(empId), GetAssignedPlansForHeadquarters(addr), DeletePlan(planId), CancelAllDeliveriesForAddress(addr), ShutdownBusiness(addr). Plan static: LogisticsManagerPlan.CalculateMaxDestinations(addr,empId), GetMaxPossibleDestinations(addr), OnFinishedDeliveries(), PendingTransactions.
Note: PricingManagerHelper.AddPlan is public; LogisticsManager plans are added by the UI doing SaveGameManager.Current.logisticsManagerPlans.Add(...) directly (no helper Add).

modFeasibility:
The Logistics/Pricing pattern is the right conceptual model but it is almost entirely NON-native for a mod, because every load-bearing piece is hard-coded into the base game rather than data/extension-driven:

NATIVE (no Harmony) — what a mod CAN reuse directly:
- Reading/writing existing game state every tick via GlobalEvents.onNewDay / a per-hour poll: enumerate SaveGameManager.Current.BuildingRegistrations, mutate reg.scheduleDays[].workShifts (ScheduleAutoFiller), mutate reg's DeliveryContract, call GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe, Notifications.Show, Contact.SendMessage. This is exactly what the existing StoreManagerMod already does.
- Hiring a real employee: EmployeeHelper.CreateAIEmployeeInstance(existingSkillName) + HireCandidate, assign assignedAddress, auto-schedule. If you reuse an EXISTING manager skill (e.g. ba:skill_logisticsmanager) the game will even instantiate the right subclass and there is already an HQ desk whose suitableSkills covers it.
- Copying the "top the store up to a per-product target from a source" delivery logic in your own code (the algorithm in LogisticsManagerPlanDestination.ProcessStockTarget is simple: target - CountTotalResourcesInStock, move that much).

NEEDS HARMONY:
- Getting your role to run off the same hooks (GameManager Hour==2 / PricingManagerHelper.RunHourly) or off EmployeeInstance.WorkDaily for a non-HRManager subclass.
- Making a custom employee subclass come out of RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate.
- Enforcing a skill-scaled store cap that the schedule UI respects.
- Auto-detaching your plan when the manager is unscheduled (mirror ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans).

NEEDS ASSET BUNDLE (prefab/ScriptableObject) — effectively infeasible to do faithfully:
- A new BizMan HQ tab ("StoreManagers") — the tab list and every panel (PlanList, PlanUI, DestinationUI, ProductCellView, NoManagerAssignedPopUp) are Unity prefabs wired in BizManBusiness; SetUpTabs() hard-codes the names. No native hook adds a tab.
- A new ba:skill_storemanager skill + a matching HQ "manager desk" item whose suitableSkills contains it (so the manager can be scheduled). Skills and items are ScriptableObject catalog data.
- Persistence of a mod-defined StoreManagerPlan: GameInstance's plan lists are fixed fields; the OdinSerializer save has no extension point. The mod must keep its own JSON side-file keyed by a stable id (building Address / employee id), exactly as the current mod's StoreManagerData does, and reconcile on load — there is no way to ride the real save.

Practical recommendation: keep the mod's own JSON-file persistence and its own onNewDay loop (native), model the plan on LogisticsManagerPlanDestination (explicit per-store list + per-product/`budget` limit fields), drive "stocked via delivery" by editing each store's real DeliveryContract (native, visible in the Deliveries tab) rather than simulating vehicles, and surface everything through Notifications + a Contact thread + the existing ModOptions panel. Reuse an existing manager skill so hiring/scheduling/desk all work natively; only reach for Harmony if you need the plan to auto-clear on unschedule or to hook the exact game tick.
